Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval containing $0$. For an integer $r\ge1$, $C^r$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through total order $r$ exist and are continuous. Let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open reference region whose boundary is, near each boundary point and in coordinates $y=Qx+c$ for some $Q\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ and $c\in\mathbb R^3$ with $Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_3$, the graph of a $C^1$ function; let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline B\subset U$. A smooth motion is a map $\chi:I\times U\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ such that, for every $t\in I$, the map $\chi_t(a):=\chi(t,a)$ is a bijection from $U$ onto an open set $\chi_t(U)$ with a $C^2$ inverse and with $\det D_a\chi(t,a)>0$ for all $a\in U$. The coordinate $a$ labels a reference point and $x=\chi(t,a)$ is its current position; $\Omega:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$ is the swept open set and $\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$ is the current image of $B$.

For $(t,x)\in\Omega$, define the inverse label $A(t,x)$ by $\chi(t,A(t,x))=x$, and put $F(t,a):=D_a\chi(t,a)$ and $J(t,a):=\det F(t,a)$. The joint map $H(t,a):=(t,\chi(t,a))$ is injective and has block-triangular derivative with determinant $J(t,a)>0$. The Euclidean inverse function theorem therefore gives local $C^1$ inverses; they agree on overlaps because the label is unique, so $A$ is globally $C^1$ on $\Omega$. Define the Eulerian velocity field $u(t,x):=\partial_t\chi(t,A(t,x))$; an Eulerian field is a function of time and current position. Thus $u$ is $C^1$.

For any $C^1$ scalar or vector field $f$ on $\Omega$, its material derivative is $D_tf:=\partial_tf+(D_xf)u$, componentwise; it is the derivative along the curves $t\mapsto\chi(t,a)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement. > For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by > $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that > $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

A bounded $C^1$ domain is a nonempty bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ whose boundary is locally, after a rigid change of coordinates, the graph $z=h(y)$ of a $C^1$ function, with $\Omega$ locally exactly the subgraph $z<h(y)$.
The same chart formula restricts to a compact Borel face contained in a regular patch.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every regular chart density is continuous and strictly positive. The chart integral on a compact embedded $C^1$ hypersurface defines a finite Borel measure independent of the finite charts and subordinate partitions. In graph coordinates $X(y)=(y,h(y))$ its density is $\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$. On a one-sided domain boundary the outward unit normal agrees on chart overlaps and is continuous.

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, let $B\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open region, let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline B$, and let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U,\mathbb R^3)$ be a family of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms $\chi_t:U\to\chi_t(U)$ with $J(t,a):=\det D_a\chi(t,a)>0$. Here $C^r$ means that all coordinate partial derivatives through total order $r$ exist and are continuous; a diffeomorphism is a bijection with an inverse of the stated regularity. Write $A(t,x)=\chi_t^{-1}(x)$, $u(t,x)=\partial_t\chi(t,A(t,x))$, $F=D_a\chi$, $L=D_xu$, and $\theta=\operatorname{tr}L=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_{x_i}u_i$. Here $D_a\chi$ and $D_xu$ are matrices of coordinate partial derivatives. The joint inverse $A$ has domain $\Omega=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$.

A compact Jordan set $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ means a compact set whose boundary, for every $\varepsilon>0$, is coverable by finitely many axis-parallel boxes with total volume less than $\varepsilon$, where a box's volume is the product of its side lengths. Integrals over such sets are Riemann integrals, defined by extending the integrand by zero to a containing rectangle. Let $K\subset U$ be any compact Jordan set and let $q,\rho\in C^1(\Omega,\mathbb R)$. Then $A$ is jointly $C^2$, and for every $a\in U$ and $t\in I$,

$$\partial_tF(t,a)=L(t,\chi(t,a))F(t,a),\qquad \partial_tJ(t,a)=J(t,a)\theta(t,\chi(t,a)),\qquad J(t,a)=J(0,a)\exp\!\left(\int_0^t\theta(s,\chi(s,a))\,ds\right).$$

For every $t\in I$, change of variables and material transport satisfy

$$\int_{\chi_t(K)}q(t,x)\,dx=\int_Kq(t,\chi(t,a))J(t,a)\,da,$$

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(K)}q(t,x)\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(K)}\bigl(D_tq(t,x)+q(t,x)\theta(t,x)\bigr)\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(K)}\bigl(\partial_tq+\nabla_x\!\cdot(qu)\bigr)\,dx,$$

where $D_tq=\partial_tq+u\cdot\nabla_xq$ and $\nabla_x\!\cdot(qu)=\sum_{i=1}^3\partial_{x_i}(qu_i)$. Define $M_K(t):=\int_{\chi_t(K)}\rho(t,x)\,dx$. The pointwise continuity equation $D_t\rho+\rho\theta=0$, equivalently $\partial_t\rho+\nabla_x\!\cdot(\rho u)=0$, holds on $\Omega$ if and only if $M_K$ is constant on $I$ for every compact Jordan $K\subset U$, and if and only if $\rho(t,\chi(t,a))J(t,a)=\rho(0,\chi(0,a))J(0,a)$ for all $a\in U$ and $t\in I$. This is a mathematical equivalence; it adopts no physical mass-conservation postulate and asserts no weak-field or vacuum extension.
Then there is a unique matrix $\sigma(t,x)\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ such that $\tau(t,x,n)=\sigma(t,x)n$ for every $n\in S^2$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge2$, a bounded $C^1$ domain Omega and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$. Both integrals are finite, with the continuous interior derivative convention and the outward normal on every boundary component.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement. > For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by > $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that > $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Let $n\ge2$. A bounded $C^1$ domain is a nonempty bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ whose boundary is locally, after a rigid change of coordinates, the graph $z=h(y)$ of a $C^1$ function, with $\Omega$ locally exactly the subgraph $z<h(y)$. Connectedness is not required. The outward normal in these coordinates is $\nu=(-Dh,1)/\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$, transported by the orthogonal coordinate map.

Let $T>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $m\ge1$ be an integer. A measurable function on an open Euclidean set $D$ is locally integrable if its norm has finite Lebesgue integral on every compact subset of $D$. For a space-time field on $\Omega\times[0,T)$ this condition is imposed on compact subsets in the relative topology, including those meeting $t=0$. Fields are identified when they agree almost everywhere. Let $U: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^m$, $F: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^{m\times3}$, and $S: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^m$ be such fields, and let $U_0:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be locally integrable. For each row $a$, define $(\operatorname{div}_x F)_a=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}F_{aj}$ in the distributional sense, and define $F:\nabla_x\phi=\sum_{a=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^3F_{aj}\partial_{x_j}\phi_a$. The equation $\partial_tU+\operatorname{div}_xF=S$ with distributional initial datum $U_0$ means that for every $\phi\in C_c^1(\Omega\times[0,T);\mathbb R^m)$, continuously differentiable up to $t=0$ and supported away from $\partial\Omega$ and $t=T$,

$$\int_0^T\!\int_\Omega\bigl(U\cdot\partial_t\phi+F:\nabla_x\phi+S\cdot\phi\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega U_0(x)\cdot\phi(x,0)\,dx=0.$$

No boundary condition on $\partial\Omega$ is encoded because the test fields are supported away from it. This initial identity specifies the initial datum distributionally; it does not assert $U(\cdot,t)\to U_0$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ or any other stronger trace topology. Such a trace must be assumed or proved separately. The fields are abstract mathematical variables; no physical unit system or balance postulate is imposed.

For locally integrable scalar fields $H,R,H_0$ and a locally integrable flux $Q: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^3$, the inequality $\partial_tH+\operatorname{div}_x Q\ge R$ with initial datum $H_0$ means that for every nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^1(\Omega\times[0,T))$ with the same support convention,

$$\int_0^T\!\int_\Omega\bigl(H\,\partial_t\psi+Q\cdot\nabla_x\psi+R\psi\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega H_0(x)\psi(x,0)\,dx\le0.$$
